newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Three S.Korean banks under review - rating agency.
newsitem.headline: Three S.Korean banks under review - rating agency.

text.p: Cyprus-based Capital Intelligence has placed the credit ratings of three South Korean banks under review for its exposure to the Hanbo conglomerate which started to default on loan payments last week.

The specialist bank credit rating agency said in a press release it was placing Cho Hung Bank (rated A long-term, A-1 short-term), Korea Exchange Bank (A, A-1) and Korea First Bank (BBB+, A-1), under review.

The three banks have significant exposure to the Hanbo Group. The steel company which forms the core of the Hanbo conglomerate began to default on loan payments last Thursday, and at least three members of the group were expected to apply for court receivership this week.
Hanbo ranks fourteenth among South Koreas's largest companies, with assets of over $6.5 billion.
Capital Intelligence said it reaffirmed its ratings for another major lender to Hanbo, Korea Development Bank (AA, A-1 +) which is wholly owned and guaranteed by the Korean government.
Hanbo's banks are reported to have agreed to reinstate credit facilities for the group, in order to avoid a collapse, and it is hoped that it can be sold as a going concern.

Nevertheless, the three main commercial bank lenders all suffer from a considerable burden of non-performing loans and further heavy provisioning requirements resulting from Hanbo's failure would add to their problems.
Capital Intelligence said it was monitoring developments closely and would decide on any possible ratings changes on the banks concerned as the situation becomes clearer.
